Bucket policy on the S3 bucket granting the Elastic Load Balancing log delivery service (logdelivery.elasticloadbalancing.amazonaws.com) permission to write logs

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amplify/late.goal: Create an S3 bucket policy that grants Amplify Hosting permission to list and retrieve objects, so a static website can be deployed from S3 to Amplify Hosting using the AWS SDKs

Destination S3 bucket for the export, which must not be publicly accessible or Requester Pays; MGN does not create it

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/lates.goal: Grant users in a different AWS account (Account B) access, via Athena queries, to an Amazon S3 bucket in Account A, including a bucket encrypted with a custom AWS KMS key, using bucket policies, KMS key policies and IAM role policies.

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/lat.goal: Transfer data from on-premises storage to an Amazon S3 bucket in a different AWS account using AWS DataSync (agent and task in the source account, bucket in the destination account)

prerequisites.what: Source account user permissions (IAM role/identity policy) allowing the user to create DataSync agents, locations and tasks
Destination account user permissions allowing the user to update the destination bucket policy and disable ACLs
Destination S3 bucket in the destination account
DataSync agent deployed on-premises and activated in the source account
IAM role in the source account (source-datasync-role) that DataSync assumes to write to the destination bucket
Inline IAM policy on the DataSync role granting S3 access to the destination bucket
Destination bucket policy granting the source account's DataSync role access to the bucket
ACLs disabled on the destination bucket (Object Ownership) so the destination account owns the data

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/detective/la.goal: Attach the required IAM permissions policy to your IAM identity so that Detective can be integrated with Amazon Security Lake

prerequisites.what: An IAM identity (role) in the account to which the inline policy is attached
Permission to attach IAM policies to the IAM identity (otherwise contact the AWS administrator)
Optional Amazon S3 bucket for storing Athena query results (if you do not want Detective to generate one automatically)

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/lates.goal: Set up an Amazon S3 bucket with the required bucket policy so Capacity Manager can deliver data exports to it

prerequisites.what: An Amazon S3 bucket in the reader's AWS account to receive and store Capacity Manager export files (existing or newly created)

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamo.goal: Export DynamoDB table data to an Amazon S3 bucket (full, incremental, or filtered export) using the console, AWS CLI, or SDKs

prerequisites.what: Point-in-time recovery (PITR) enabled on the source table
Destination Amazon S3 bucket that the reader can write to (not requester pays; may be in another Region or account)
IAM identity-based policy allowing s3:AbortMultipartUpload, s3:PutObject, s3:PutObjectAcl and dynamodb:ExportTableToPointInTime
Bucket policy on the destination bucket allowing the exporting principal to write (required for cross-account buckets or buckets the reader lacks permission to write to)
IAM role in the table's account to assume when exporting a table owned by another account (export request must come from the table's account)

KMS customer managed key with key policy permitting DynamoDB use via the exporting IAM user/role (only if the table or bucket is encrypted with a customer managed key; must be in the same Region as the destination bucket)

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/u.goal: Configure IAM permissions for the EKS ACK capability by using IAM Role Selectors (including cross-account) to map service-specific IAM roles to namespaces

prerequisites.what: Existing ACK capability with its Capability Role (IAM role) that will assume the service-specific roles
Trust policy on the service-specific IAM role allowing the Capability Role to assume it
Target account (444455556666) cross-account IAM role trusting the source account's Capability Role, with service permissions attached
Kubernetes namespaces (e.g. s3-resources, production) to which the IAMRoleSelector maps roles

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emr/latest/M.goal: Set up a security configuration with IAM roles for EMRFS so that EMRFS requests to Amazon S3 assume different IAM roles based on user, group, or S3 prefix

prerequisites.what: IAM roles for EMRFS, each with a permissions policy granting the desired S3 access (plan and create before setting up the security configuration)
Trust policy on each EMRFS role allowing the cluster's Amazon EMR role for EC2 (EMR_EC2_DefaultRole) to assume it
Trust policy statement on the Amazon EMR role for EC2 (EMR_EC2_DefaultRole) allowing the EMRFS roles to assume it
Role specified as a key user in the KMS key policy, if the role accesses S3 data encrypted with an AWS KMS key
Custom Amazon EMR role for EC2 (instance profile) with restricted S3 permissions, to be used instead of the default as the fallback role when creating the cluster

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emr/latest/E.goal: Run EMR Serverless Spark batch or interactive jobs that read and write Lake Formation-protected Glue Data Catalog tables using full table access (FTA) mode

prerequisites.what: Lake Formation setting allowing third-party query engines to access data without IAM session tag validation (full table access application integration), enabled in both producer and consumer accounts/regions for cross-account or cross-region access
Job runtime role with IAM permissions including lakeformation:GetDataAccess, Glue API permissions, and S3 access for the script and logs (user-defined role, not a service-linked role)
IAM identity policy for the job runtime role granting lakeformation:GetDataAccess, Glue, and S3 permissions
Lake Formation permissions granted to the job runtime role on the Data Catalog resources (SELECT for reads, ALL/SUPER for writes/deletes, DESCRIBE/ALTER/DROP as needed)
AWS Glue Data Catalog configured as the Spark metastore for EMR Serverless

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElasti.goal: Export an ElastiCache (Valkey/Redis OSS) backup to an Amazon S3 bucket so it can be accessed outside ElastiCache

prerequisites.what: Amazon S3 bucket in the same AWS Region as the backup, with a DNS-compliant name, to receive the exported backup
S3 bucket policy granting the ElastiCache service access (object read/write and permissions read) to the target bucket
IAM identity policy for the caller allowing elasticache:CopySnapshot and S3 access to the target bucket (including s3:ListAllMyBuckets on all resources)
An existing ElastiCache backup (snapshot) to export, not using data tiering and of a supported type (not node-based Memcached)

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadb.goal: Enable connection logs for an Application Load Balancer so that Elastic Load Balancing delivers log files to an S3 bucket

prerequisites.what: S3 bucket in the same Region as the load balancer, using SSE-S3 encryption, to store connection logs
Bucket policy on the S3 bucket granting Elastic Load Balancing (log delivery service) permission to write connection logs, with the resource ARN including the load balancer account ID and any prefix

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emr/latest/M.goal: Configure an Amazon EMR cluster to archive its log files to Amazon S3 (optionally encrypted with a KMS key, or aggregated) so they can be used for debugging

prerequisites.what: Amazon S3 bucket/location to store the cluster logs (the S3 log path given in the console or --log-uri)
Default Amazon EMR service role and EC2 instance profile (create with aws emr create-default-roles) for CLI cluster launch
EC2 key pair (myKey) used in the CLI create-cluster command
AWS KMS customer managed key for encrypting logs (optional, only for log encryption)
EC2 instance profile permission for kms:GenerateDataKey and EMR role permission for kms:DescribeKey (optional, for log encryption)

KMS key policy adding the EC2 instance profile and EMR role as key users, and allowing the elasticmapreduce and persistentappui.elasticmapreduce service principals to use GenerateDataKey, GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext and Decrypt (optional, for log encryption)
Configuration file myConfig.json enabling log aggregation (only for the log aggregation procedure)

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emr/latest/E.goal: Configure Amazon EMR Serverless jobs running in one AWS account (AccountA) to access Amazon S3 data in a bucket owned by another AWS account (AccountB), using either an S3 bucket policy or an assumed IAM role.

prerequisites.what: An Amazon EMR Serverless application in AccountA where the jobs will run
A job execution role (Job-Execution-Role-A) in AccountA with the permissions required to run jobs in the application
An S3 bucket in AccountB that holds the data the EMR Serverless jobs will access

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/entityresolu.goal: Create an IAM workflow job role that AWS Entity Resolution uses to run a workflow, using the IAM console

prerequisites.what: IAM permissions to create roles (iam:CreateRole) and sign in to the IAM console with an administrator account, or an administrator who can create the role
Input Amazon S3 buckets holding the underlying data objects of the AWS Glue tables that Entity Resolution reads from
Output Amazon S3 bucket(s) where Entity Resolution writes output data
AWS Glue input databases (and tables) that Entity Resolution reads from
Customer managed KMS key(s) used to encrypt the input S3 data (only if the input is encrypted)
Customer managed KMS key(s) for encrypting the output data (only if output encryption is needed)
AWS Data Exchange subscription with a provider service, with dataset, revision and asset IDs (only for provider service-based workflows)

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accel.goal: Enable flow logs for an AWS Global Accelerator accelerator so that flow log records are published to an Amazon S3 bucket

prerequisites.what: Amazon S3 bucket in the reader's account to receive the flow logs
IAM policy for the user or role enabling flow logs, with permissions for globalaccelerator, logs and s3 actions

S3 bucket policy allowing the log delivery service to publish flow logs (added automatically if the creator owns the bucket and has GetBucketPolicy/PutBucketPolicy; otherwise the bucket owner must add it manually)
KMS key policy statement allowing flow logs to write to the bucket, required if the bucket uses SSE-KMS with a customer-managed key

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/forecast/lat.goal: Create an IAM role and an IAM policy that let Amazon Forecast list, read and write data in an Amazon S3 bucket on the reader's behalf, then attach the policy to the role

prerequisites.what: An existing Amazon S3 bucket that holds the time-series data. Its name goes into the IAM policy in place of 'bucket-name'.

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/.goal: Create an IAM role that AWS Glue can assume to call other services (such as Amazon S3) on the user's behalf, for crawlers, jobs, and development endpoints

prerequisites.what: IAM policy granting access to the specific Amazon S3 sources and targets (s3:ListBucket, s3:GetObject for sources; s3:ListBucket, s3:PutObject, s3:DeleteObject for targets), or the managed AmazonS3FullAccess policy, attached to the role
Policy allowing Glue crawlers, jobs, and development endpoints to decrypt data in SSE-KMS encrypted S3 sources/targets (only if using SSE-KMS)
iam:PassRole policy for the role, needed if the role name does not start with AWSGlueServiceRole or when the role is used with notebooks/interactive sessions
Permissions to use the IAM console and create roles (signed-in AWS account access)

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/.goal: Set up IAM permissions for AWS Glue by granting IAM identities access to Glue resources and S3 locations, and choosing or creating a default AWS Glue service role, using the Glue console.

prerequisites.what: AWS Management Console access (sign-in) with permissions to open the AWS Glue console and apply IAM changes
Existing IAM users or roles to receive AWS Glue permissions (the identities chosen in the wizard)
Amazon S3 locations (buckets/prefixes) to grant the identities access to
If choosing an existing IAM role as the default Glue service role: that role must already be configured as a Glue service role (with the IAM policy and trust relationship for Glue)
If choosing an existing IAM role as the default Glue service role: an IAM policy for the AWS Glue service attached to that role

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/omics/latest.goal: Export HealthOmics read sets from a sequence store to an Amazon S3 bucket as a batch export job

prerequisites.what: Destination Amazon S3 bucket for the exported read sets
IAM identity-based policy granting write access (s3) to the destination bucket
IAM role (referenced by role ARN) that HealthOmics assumes to write to the bucket, with a trust policy for the service principal allowing sts:AssumeRole

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/la.goal: Configure GuardDuty to export generated findings to an Amazon S3 bucket encrypted with an AWS KMS key

prerequisites.what: Amazon S3 bucket to receive exported findings (in the same Region as the KMS key)
AWS KMS key (same Region as the S3 bucket) used to encrypt exported findings
KMS key policy statement allowing GuardDuty to use the key to encrypt findings
S3 bucket policy allowing GuardDuty to upload objects (and get bucket location) in the bucket
Permissions for the user or role configuring the export: s3:GetBucketLocation and s3:PutObject (plus s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket if using a prefix), in addition to GuardDuty permissions
Existing folder structure (optional prefix and /AWSLogs/account-ID/GuardDuty/Region path) in the S3 bucket, since GuardDuty does not create folders

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/inspector/la.goal: Export an Amazon Inspector findings report (CSV or JSON) to an Amazon S3 bucket, encrypted with an AWS KMS key

prerequisites.what: IAM permissions for Amazon Inspector, AWS KMS and Amazon S3 actions needed to export reports and configure the bucket and key (e.g. inspector2:CreateFindingsReport, kms:PutKeyPolicy, s3:PutBucketPolicy)
Amazon S3 bucket to store the findings report, in the same Region as the findings data (existing or newly created; the reader must create it if it doesn't exist)
S3 bucket policy statement allowing the Amazon Inspector service principal to add objects to the bucket
Customer managed symmetric encryption AWS KMS key in the same Region as the S3 bucket (existing or newly created)
KMS key policy statement allowing Amazon Inspector to use the key to encrypt the report

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot-sitewise.goal: Create an AWS IoT SiteWise bulk import job with the AWS CLI to transfer data from Amazon S3 into AWS IoT SiteWise

prerequisites.what: AWS IoT SiteWise warm tier or cold tier storage enabled
Amazon S3 data bucket containing the data (CSV file object) to import
Amazon S3 bucket (with prefix) to receive errors from the bulk import job
IAM role that allows AWS IoT SiteWise to read the S3 data and write errors to the error bucket
IAM identity-based permissions policy on the role granting S3 access to the data bucket and error bucket
Bulk import job configuration file (JSON) referenced by the command

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot-sitewise.goal: Create a bulk import job in AWS IoT SiteWise Scenario Discovery to ingest MP4 video, Parquet telemetry, and annotation files from S3 using the CreateBulkImportJob API.

prerequisites.what: S3 bucket(s) holding the source data files to ingest, plus an S3 location for per-file error reports (may be the same bucket)
IAM role (jobRoleArn) that AWS IoT SiteWise assumes to read source objects and write error reports, with a trust policy allowing iotsitewise.amazonaws.com
Permission policy on the job role granting AWS IoT SiteWise S3 access to the source and error-report locations
Caller's IAM identity (user or role) with permission to invoke CreateBulkImportJob and iam:PassRole on the job role (with iam:PassedToService condition)
Trust policy for the caller's application role so an EC2, ECS, or Lambda workload can assume it (only if the caller is an application role)
Scenario Discovery dataset (datasetId) and workspace (workspaceName) that the import targets

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/lates.goal: Create a Lambda Event Function and configure an Amazon S3 trigger so the function runs whenever an object is added to a bucket, then test it and check its output in CloudWatch Logs

prerequisites.what: Amazon S3 bucket (in the same Region as the function) to act as the trigger event source
IAM permissions policy (s3-trigger-tutorial) allowing the function to get objects from S3 and write to CloudWatch Logs
Lambda execution role (lambda-s3-trigger-role) with the permissions policy attached
Test object uploaded to the S3 bucket, used for the dummy-event test

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/lates.goal: Create a Lambda function that resizes images uploaded to an S3 source bucket and writes thumbnails to a destination bucket, triggered by S3 events

prerequisites.what: AWS CLI installed (latest version), needed only if following the CLI path
Language support tools and package manager for Python or Node.js
Command line terminal or shell able to run commands such as zip (on Windows, WSL)
Source S3 bucket for uploading images
Destination S3 bucket (source name plus -resized) for thumbnails, in the same Region
IAM permissions policy (LambdaS3Policy) granting S3 read/write and CloudWatch Logs access
Lambda execution role (LambdaS3Role) with the permissions policy attached

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/d.goal: Configure AWS IoT rules in one account (Account A) so MQTT messages are routed to an Amazon SQS queue, Amazon SNS topic, Amazon S3 bucket or AWS Lambda function in another account (Account B), using resource-based permissions on the destination

prerequisites.what: AWS CLI installed and configured with IAM user credentials for Account A (and later Account B)
Account B Amazon SQS queue (ExampleQueue) as the destination
Account A IAM user permissions for iot:CreateTopicRule (on the rule ARN) and iam:PassRole (on the role ARN) for the SQS rule
Account A IAM role trusted by the AWS IoT rules engine with a policy allowing access to Account B's SQS queue
Account B Amazon SNS topic (ExampleTopic) as the destination
Account A IAM user permissions for iot:CreateTopicRule (on the rule ARN) and iam:PassRole (on the role ARN) for the SNS rule
Account A IAM role trusted by the AWS IoT rules engine with a policy allowing access to Account B's SNS topic
Account B Amazon S3 bucket as the destination
Account A IAM user permissions for iot:CreateTopicRule (on the rule ARN) and iam:PassRole (on the role ARN) for the S3 rule
Account A IAM role trusted by the AWS IoT rules engine with a policy allowing access to Account B's S3 bucket
Correct S3 Block all public access settings on the bucket so cross-account access works
Account B Lambda function (example-function) as the destination
Account A IAM user permissions for iot:CreateTopicRule (on the rule ARN) and iam:PassRole (on the role ARN) for the Lambda rule
Account B IAM user permission for lambda:AddPermission
